name: 手打ちそば 創愿 (Teuchi Soba Sougen)

claims.text: Wheat-containing niwari (80% buckwheat / 20% wheat) and sarashina soba are made in the same kitchen as the juwari (100% buckwheat) soba; shared surfaces and equipment are likely.
The tsuyu is built on a 20-year-old kaeshi made with Shinshu shoyu — standard Japanese soy sauce brewed with wheat. All broth-based and dipping dishes will contain wheat-derived soy sauce.
Tempura is on the menu, meaning wheat-batter frying takes place in the kitchen. Duck (kamo) and pork dipping broths are signature items, so animal products are central to the cooking environment.
No allergy menu, allergy statement, or staff allergy-handling protocol has been published on any source reviewed. Guests with serious allergies should call 052-951-1226 before visiting.
Juwari soba (十割そば, 100% buckwheat, no wheat flour in the noodle itself) is a standing menu option and represents a genuine wheat-free noodle choice for those avoiding gluten by preference.

name: Vegedeco Salad Lab (ベジデコサラダラボ)

claims.text: Shop replaces wheat flour entirely with 大豆粉 (soy flour) and 米粉 (rice flour); the full product line is wheat-free, but no explicit celiac cross-contact protocol is published.
Sweets/salad-cake shop — soy sauce is not a primary ingredient; sweetening is via 甘麹 (fermented rice koji), not sugar or wheat-based seasoning.
Mixed line — some items use eggs (さつまいもタルト) and honey (soufflé), so vegan and non-vegan items are produced in the same kitchen.
No specific allergy-handling statement published; company does gluten-free menu consulting, suggesting allergen awareness. Confirm by phone (052-753-7775).
Entire menu is wheat-free using soy/rice flour; internationally recognised gluten-free specialist (CNN, BBC).
Fully wheat-free premises — the guide rates every product gluten-free (★★★★★) and the shop states its bread uses no wheat flour and is made from whole rice, so flour cross-contact is minimal.
Breads are egg/dairy/soy-milk-free, but dairy-based items (cheese balls, cheesecake) are made in the same kitchen; vegans should ask which items contain dairy.
Shop's own statement: 「パンは卵、牛乳、豆乳、小麦粉、砂糖不使用です。米粉ではなくお米から作っています」
All products gluten-free; ★★★★★ celiac rating in a curated Japanese GF guide.

name: エニー ビー&ビー+コーヒー（ANY B&B+COFFEE） (ANY B&B + COFFEE)

claims.text: Not a dedicated gluten-free kitchen; wheat-based hot sandwiches and toast are prepared in the same small cafe, so cross-contact is possible for celiacs.
Dairy and egg/cheese items (e.g., egg-and-cheese sandwiches, cow's milk) are handled in the same space, so vegan items are made in a non-vegan environment.
Offers a daily-rotating selection of gluten-free and vegan baked goods and sweets alongside house-made granola.
Provides non-dairy (alternative) milk options for coffee drinks.
Melbourne-trained, English-comfortable owners make it easy to ask about ingredients.

name: Big Mountain Cafe＆Farm（ビッグマウンテン カフェ＆ファーム） (Big Mountain Cafe & Farm)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free menu document or cross-contamination / dedicated-fryer protocol is published; HappyCow's listing notes no specific celiac safety information is provided.
The cafe makes house soy-sauce koji (醤油糀) and uses fermented seasonings; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so confirm which seasoning is used on a given dish if strictly avoiding gluten.
Kitchen is not exclusively vegan — it also prepares meat, seafood and egg dishes (loco moco, garlic shrimp, oxtail soup), so vegan diners should order from the clearly marked vegan items.
Allergy accommodations are arranged at the time of reservation against an allergen list; same-day changes cannot be accommodated.
The vegan variety lunch plate requires advance reservation.
Built as a gluten-free kitchen: all sweets are gluten-free and they bake gluten-free burgers, buns, fried chicken and fries.
English menu available with vegan and gluten-free items clearly identified, aiding diners with dietary restrictions.
Listed by Find Me Gluten Free as a dedicated gluten-free restaurant in Nara and recommended for those with dietary restrictions.

name: café komorebi（カフェ こもれ陽） (café komorebi (kafe komorebi))

claims.text: The house salad dressing is made with gluten-free soy sauce rather than standard wheat-based shoyu.
The owner built the cafe specifically to accommodate gluten allergies, vegetarian, vegan, halal and kosher diets, so staff are oriented around dietary needs.
Signature focaccia is made from Hinohikari rice flour with no wheat.
Seasonal anmitsu uses plant-based gelato made without dairy or eggs (brown-rice/soy/coconut-milk base).
Profile states the cafe is gluten-free, halal and kosher friendly with fresh vegetables and herbs.

name: coffret café（コフレカフェ） (Coffret Cafe)

claims.text: The kitchen prepares wheat-based French toast, cakes and pastries alongside the 100% buckwheat galette, and no gluten-free segregation is documented, so cross-contamination is likely.
Menu is built around dairy and eggs (milk/butter/egg French toast and cheesecakes); no documented separation for plant-based diners.
The signature lunch galette uses 100% buckwheat flour, a naturally gluten-free grain, which is a genuine option for gluten-avoiders who confirm details in person.

name: HALAL & VEGGIE Restaurant ポンテロッソ (HALAL & VEGGIE Restaurant Ponte Rosso)

claims.text: Curries are labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free naan can be made on advance request, but standard wheat naan is baked on-site, so the kitchen is not a dedicated gluten-free environment and cross-contact is possible.
Halal meat dishes are prepared in the same kitchen as the vegan and vegetarian items, so diners should specify the vegan version (e.g., vegan dal bhat) when ordering.

The kitchen explicitly avoids animal fats, commercial oils, and additives, and offers dedicated halal, vegetarian, and vegan dishes, indicating staff routinely accommodate dietary needs; specific allergen protocols were not documented, so confirm by phone (0742-23-0808).
Dedicated vegan dal bhat, vegan biryani, and plant-based yogurt are on the menu, plus naan made without egg, milk, or baking powder.
All meat is halal-certified, and sweets are made with cane sugar instead of white sugar.
